proposed_rules: A frame declares entity grain and identity; a chart declares mark identity and measure aggregation.
A many-side traversal offers aggregation at the current grain or a deliberate frame change.
An ambiguous unique lookup cannot choose the first match; unresolved fields/measures remain visibly unavailable until resolved.
Collapse duplicate entity marks only where the chart identity permits it; measure aggregation still follows declared grain.
A chart shows query glyph, frame/measure meaning, and included/available count; inspection exposes expansion and distinct entity counts when relevant.
A query glyph identifies its definition; labels and details identify active bindings and frame. Source glyphs identify contributing tables.
Automatic parameter updates publish consistent stage results; pending results retain their applied labels until replaced.
Host persistence restores investigation state; derived rows may recompute from the same definitions and source references.
shape.problem: A flat row array hides table relationships, query paths, and the rows produced by intermediate steps.

ownership.renderer: Chart-specific mark identity and measure rules over selected results; never deduplicate all joins indiscriminately.

scale_probe.latency: seconds; rough user estimate, no precise SLA
scale_probe.status: Measured and accepted with one local worker
scale_probe.proof: Probe indexed local execution and serialization in milestone 2. In milestone 4 measure fixed-seed ten-table/10,000-row inputs, fan-out, result rows, origin size, browser responsiveness, and persisted size. Use a worker only if measurements require it; never silently truncate computed rows.
evidence: Node24 fixed-seed probe: ten10000-row sources;10000resultrows,100000 origin links.196ms cold,242/178ms warm;41ms serialization;2,482,460 compactbytes.20000-row expansion39ms;10000ambiguities233ms.
Reproduce: node packages/explorEDA/scripts/probe-analysis.ts tmp/analysis-scale.exploreda-project.json. Browser proof remains in exp-1iuz.
Browser input-to-frame delay was 447–1,006 ms on the fixed-seed parameter query. Long Tasks matched those delays. This meets the plan’s worker condition; final responsiveness proof remains required.

Final Node 24 probe: seed 42; 100,000 input rows; 10,000 output rows; 100,000 origin links. Cold evaluation took 178 ms; warm runs took 158 and 150 ms. Aggregation reduced 10,000 rows to 1,001 groups in 18 ms. Independent group count and sum checks passed. Serialization took 36 ms and produced 2,482,460 compact bytes. Origins used 6,097,801 bytes. A 20,000-row expansion took 41 ms; 10,000 ambiguous rows took 274 ms.

Real browser worker timings: input-to-frame delay was about 75–100 ms without a chart and 125–128 ms with a chart. Final result application took about 625 ms and 479 ms, respectively. Chart warmup had one 344 ms task. Rapid bindings finished on minimum 900 with 1,031 rows and matching applied labels and stage counts. The pre-worker input delay was 447–1,006 ms. These measurements are local observations, not a service guarantee.
